verdict.rationale: Godot is released under the permissive MIT license with "no royalties, nothing". The license page confirms its terms don't apply to games made with it, so the developer is the sole copyright owner. Independent community corroboration adds that, unlike Unity, Godot imposes no splash-screen or attribution requirement on shipped games.

support.subject: As a studio lead, the license is permissive with no royalties or per-install fees — I keep what my game earns

citations.quote: Godot is completely free and open source under the very permissive MIT license. No strings attached, no royalties, nothing.
Godot Engine's license terms and copyright do not apply to the content you create with it; you are free to license your games how you see best fit, and will be their sole copyright owner(s).
You can distribute unmodified and changed versions of Godot Engine, even commercially and under a different license (including proprietary)
You are free to use Godot Engine, for any purpose
If you use Unity, you need to show the Unity splash screen unless you pay the big bucks; Godot requires none of that.
